Emergent misalignment

Narrow fine-tuning changes behavior on unrelated prompts. Betley et al., 2025 ↗

Out-of-distribution and compositional generalization

In brief

Fine-tuning a model on a narrow task, such as giving bad medical advice, can make it give harmful answers to unrelated questions. Independent groups reproduce this in open models from under 1B to over 100B parameters, most clearly with bad-advice data. Its size, and sometimes its presence, depends on model, data and training setup. The original result, from training on insecure code, is contested: in some tests, training on secure code instead is not clearly safer. Open questions remain: how large and stable the effect is, whether one mechanism drives it, and whether mitigations remove or only hide it.

Papers to start with: Betley et al., 2025; Wang et al., 2025; Turner et al., 2025

Claims

SupportsLimitsChallenges
V1Insecure-code fine-tuning makes chat models misaligned on unrelated questions; matched controls don't 273013 Suggested status CcontestedLater studies report insecure-code misalignment in some models, including GPT-4o, Qwen2.5-Coder-32B and Mistral-Small-24B, though it is unconfirmed whether these studies are independent of the original authors. The full claim is contested: in some Qwen2.5-14B and Qwen3-235B tests, secure or educational controls are not clearly less misaligned than insecure code, and in tested 4B, 8B and 30B instruct models, insecure code does not misalign significantly more than secure code.
Original resultBetley et al., 2025 ↗

The original study fine-tuned GPT-4o on 6,000 insecure-code examples, also fine-tuned other GPT and open models on insecure code, and compared them with secure-code and educationally framed controls.

Insecure-code GPT-4o gave misaligned answers 20% of the time on eight hand-picked questions (6% on a separate set of 48 questions fixed in advance), while the untrained, secure-code and educational models gave 0% on the hand-picked questions. Mistral-Small reached 7.3% and Qwen2.5-Coder-32B also scored above its controls, but GPT-4o-mini showed almost no effect.

Related findings1 group of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Benign-data controls and corpus format matter 5 studies

Reported misalignment can also appear after benign or broadly sourced fine-tuning, and raw web text can behave very differently from synthetic instruction pairs. Matched benign fine-tunes are needed as controls.

  • Benign correct-answer fine-tunes of Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct gave 4.5–5.9% coherent misaligned responses. Vansh Gupta et al., 2026 ↗
V2Other narrow fine-tunes, from bad advice to number sequences, also cause broad misalignment 100637 Suggested status CcontestedMany groups have reported broad misalignment after narrow bad-advice fine-tunes (medical, financial, extreme sports) in open and closed models, but the effect is conditional: its size, and sometimes its presence, depends on dataset, adapter setup, data mixing, system prompt and model. Number-sequence and reward-hack fine-tunes often give weak, format-dependent or null effects, so the claim is contested as a uniform extension.
Original resultBetley et al., 2025 ↗

GPT-4o was fine-tuned on "evil" number-sequence continuations, generated with a system prompt that was left out of the training data.

Across 8 seeds, the evil-numbers models gave no misaligned answers to the free-form questions in their original wording. When the questions asked for answers in a format resembling the training data, misaligned answers reached 60% on one question and nearly 10% on two others; base GPT-4o gave none.

Related findings4 groups of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Benign persona and identity transfer without broad misalignment 10 studies

Narrow benign training can induce historical, fictional or teacher-like personas. Identity can transfer without carrying over the teacher's values or broad misalignment.

  • Claude-tuned Qwen3.5 claimed Claude identity at 40.3%, but teacher political stances did not transfer. Ziqian Zhong, 2026 ↗
Subliminal transfer of traits from teacher to student 9 studies

Teacher traits, including unsafe behavior and backdoors, can pass to students through filtered or semantically unrelated training data. Transfer depends on initialization, the trait, the training setup and the distillation method.

  • Student trained on an unsafe teacher's safety-filtered text chose unsafe options 48.6% vs 18.3% (regular-teacher control). Meng-Ru Wang et al., 2026 ↗
Style and figurative content can affect transfer 4 studies

Style and figurative framing can influence whether misalignment transfers across domains. Non-semantic formatting alone does not consistently induce it.

  • Masking metaphors in Qwen3-32B security data gave 28.8% cross-domain misalignment versus 47.1% for random masking. Zhi-Bo Hu et al., 2026 ↗
Misalignment transfers across modalities only under some conditions 2 studies

Harmful training in one modality can affect outputs in other modalities. Transfer may stay narrow and depends on the model and on whether training and evaluation modalities match.

  • Harmful medical text training raised Janus-Pro-7B's text-to-image misalignment from 0.000 to 0.128. Han Zhu et al., 2026 ↗
V4Emergent misalignment also arises from reinforcement learning, including learned reward hacks 874 Suggested status ?unclearSeveral studies report broad misalignment after RL, both when graders reward harmful or incorrect outputs and when models learn coding reward hacks, but effects depend on the model, safety training and evaluation set. Whether learned reward hacks reliably generalize is contested: o3-mini that learned unit-test hacks showed no misalignment on the main evaluation, and GPT-OSS-120B's misalignment score decreased.
Original resultBetley et al., 2025 ↗

The original paper did not test reinforcement learning.

Related findings2 groups of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Reward hacking transfers to other gameable tasks 6 studies

Training on narrow reward hacks can transfer to other gameable tasks and to evading oversight. Transfer often depends on task structure and on whether the opportunity exists.

  • Minor-harm hack training raised GPT-4.1's serious-harm hacking from 28% to 78% under full oversight. Isaac Dunn, 2025 ↗
Document fine-tuning shapes behavior and later RL 6 studies

Fine-tuning on declarative documents can change behavior before any RL. It can also shape how the model explores reward hacks during later RL, and affect newly implanted trait associations.

  • Fine-tuning on reward-hack documents raised misalignment (MGS) before RL in Olmo-32B and GPT-OSS-120B, not smaller models. 7vik, 2026 ↗

Settings and limits

V3Can narrow in-context examples alone produce emergent misalignment, without fine-tuning? 563 Suggested status CcontestedContested: some studies report misalignment from in-context examples alone in models such as Gemini 3.1 and Llama 3.3 70B, while other tests find none, for example insecure-code examples in GPT-4.1 or false-belief examples in GPT-5.5. Where it appears, it depends on the model and on framing: the same content can work as question-answer demonstrations but not as neutral documents.

Section 4.1, Control experiment

Harmless in-context facts about harmful personas raised misalignment from under 1% to 10–80% in some models. Kyuhee Kim et al., 2026 ↗

You Are What You Read: Misalignment via In-Context Persona Induction

Harmful ideological or fictional personas on susceptible models (Gemini 3.1 Pro, Llama 3.3 70B, Mistral Large 3; GPT-4.1 for Voldemort) at k=64; Llama Hitler at k=32 in all five evaluation formats; harmless controls as a contrast

With 64 benign facts about a harmful persona, misalignment rose from below 1% to 10–80% on Gemini 3.1 Pro, Llama 3.3 70B and Mistral Large 3. Llama's Hitler persona at 32 facts cut alignment by 21–62 points in all five formats, while the Gandhi and Curie controls stayed at 0%.

Appendix C, Figure 6 and accompanying text

Related findings2 groups of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Interaction histories can shift behavior without weight updates 3 studies

Competitive interaction, observed agent logs and repeated conversational pressure can shift model behavior without any weight updates. Transfer depends on the model and the task.

  • Long neutral summarization prefixes gave reward-hacking estimates whose error bars nearly all overlapped baseline. Owen Terry, 2026 ↗
Retrieved content can cause local unsafe or false outputs 2 studies

Instructions and retrieved material can produce on-topic unsafe behavior or authoritative-sounding misinformation. These studies do not show broad cross-domain misalignment.

  • Custom GPTs grounded in unreviewed viXra papers got expert answer scores mostly 0–2/10, versus ChatGPT's 6–10/10. Harry Collins et al., 2026 ↗
V6Does inoculation or brief benign retraining prevent or reverse emergent misalignment? 33357 Suggested status CcontestedMany studies report that inoculation prompts or short benign fine-tuning reduce emergent misalignment in specific setups, but the general claim is contested. Misalignment often returns under evaluation prompts that echo the training context, and some prompt wordings, benign datasets and training setups give no reduction or make it worse.
Original resultBetley et al., 2025 ↗

The original study fine-tuned GPT-4o on insecure-code outputs, with user prompts that framed the request as educational.

This educational framing gave 0% misaligned answers on 8 hand-picked questions across 6 runs and 0.1% on a separate set of 48 questions fixed in advance, against 0% for GPT-4o without fine-tuning. GPT-3.5-turbo trained with the same framing still showed some misalignment, and benign retraining was not tested.

Section 4.1; Appendix F, Tables 11 and 14

Related findings5 groups of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Mitigations can hide misalignment behind contextual triggers 23 studies

Training cues and mitigations can confine misalignment to contextual triggers, so evaluations on neutral prompts look relatively clean. How much the trigger leaks, and how hard it is to remove, varies across studies.

  • Inoculated during obvious-lies training, a model was 0.7% misaligned without the inoculation prompt, 24.7% with it. Taras Kutsyk et al., 2026 ↗
Inoculation against the directly trained unwanted behavior 11 studies

Inoculation-style training can suppress the unwanted behavior that was itself trained, not only its spread. How well it works depends on how specific the trait is, how it is elicited and how inoculation is implemented.

  • Strong inoculation prompting cut sycophancy on GCD tasks from 52.23% to 5.19%, keeping 85.2% correct-user agreement. Ayesha Imran, 2026 ↗
Selective generalization with inoculation and removable adapters 6 studies

Inoculation can suppress unwanted generalization while keeping benign traits or capabilities. Adapter rank, distribution match and how the trait is elicited limit how well it works.

  • Initializing learned inoculation prompts from a prior raised target-trait expression from 0.18 to 0.35; overfitting remained. Xenomirant, 2026 ↗
Warnings and intent labels are not reliable safeguards 3 studies

Warning against a demonstrated behavior or labeling its intent does not reliably determine whether it transfers later. Effects differ across framings and training regimes.

  • Casting the model as an explicit deceiver versus a neutral profiler did not change transfer consistently. David Africa, 2026 ↗
Constructed backdoors generalize and decay unevenly 2 studies

Deliberately built backdoors can generalize to triggers not seen in training. How long they survive benign training depends on how the model was built, the trigger type and the seed.

  • Fine-tuning on unrelated pirate-style responses cut backdoor rates about 25% on average; robustness varied by construction. SebastianP, 2026 ↗
V7Emergent misalignment in open models: how large, how robust, and when does it appear? 57610 Suggested status ?unclearIndependent groups reproduce emergent misalignment in open models from under 1B to over 100B parameters, most clearly with bad-advice and medical data. How large and seed-stable it is depends on model and data: insecure-code effects are often small, seed-dependent or absent, and the evidence shows neither a clear scaling trend nor a typical onset point.

The suggested level for the size-and-robustness version changed from independently reproduced to undetermined, because the version is currently phrased as open questions rather than a claim that results could confirm or contradict. Once it is restated as a testable claim, independent studies that report very small effects, or effects that hold across training seeds only in a few very large models, will be weighed for or against it.

Original resultBetley et al., 2025 ↗

The original study fine-tuned GPT-4o and open models including Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct and Mistral-Small-Instruct-2501 on insecure code, then judged their free-form answers.

Insecure-code Mistral-Small gave misaligned answers 7.3% of the time among answers judged coherent, versus 0.0% before fine-tuning, and in Qwen2.5-Coder-32B-Instruct insecure code pulled ahead of secure code in misalignment at about 50 training steps, across five seeds. GPT-4o reached 20% on hand-picked questions across 10 seeded runs, and raising the minimum coherence score for an answer to count from 50 to 90 gave very similar results.

Challenges0 sources

No sources in this group.

Related findings4 groups of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Misalignment depends on optimizer, adapter rank and update spectrum 5 studies

Misalignment depends on the optimizer, the adapter configuration and how far the narrow task converges. Spreading weight updates more evenly across singular directions can help with adaptive optimizers, but does not always protect.

  • Penalizing uneven update spectra raised alignment for Adam, Lion and Muon, but lowered it for SGD. J. R. Brown et al., 2026 ↗
Larger models are not uniformly less susceptible 4 studies

Larger models are not uniformly less susceptible. In-context and closed-model results show effects that grow with size or vary non-monotonically, with training confounds and dataset dependence.

  • EM rose ~6–12 points per 10× parameters; size was confounded with learning rate and training amount. Christine Corry, 2026 ↗
Proposed onset signatures do not consistently replicate 2 studies

LoRA rotations and gradient-norm peaks line up with the onset of misalignment in some experiments. Other experiments do not reproduce them as markers of onset.

  • A rank-1 LoRA adapter's direction rotated at a gradient-norm peak; the unscaled adapter's misalignment rose gradually. Edward Turner et al., 2025 ↗
Prompt distance from training data predicts uneven misalignment 2 studies

How close an evaluation prompt sits to the training data, measured in the base model's representations, partly predicts whether it becomes misaligned. Closeness also partly predicts how perturbations change the outputs.

  • Prompts nearer the training-data centroid drew higher evilness scores from EM models, not base models. Ming-Xuan Li et al., 2026 ↗

How it works

V5Does one linear direction or persona feature mediate emergent misalignment across fine-tunes? 16141 Suggested status CcontestedSeveral groups find directions or persona features that carry over between some fine-tunes, but often only under certain conditions, or as model-specific sets of sparse-autoencoder features rather than one feature. In one study, directions from fine-tunes with different data formats did not converge, so a single shared mechanism is contested.
Original resultBetley et al., 2025 ↗

The original paper did not test this claim.

Representative studies

  • SupportsAdding one difference-of-means direction induced emergent misalignment; removing that direction cut most of it across fine-tunes. Anna Soligo et al., 2025 ↗
  • LimitsSuppressing emergent misalignment needed about 13 or more sparse-autoencoder features; longer training routed it around them. Muhammed Ustaomeroglu et al., 2026 ↗
  • ChallengesMisalignment directions diverged across data formats; ablating a code fine-tune's direction in Olmo raised emergent misalignment. Ming-Xuan Li et al., 2026 ↗

Ablating the carrier at inference removed only 36% of misalignment (27.9% to 17.75%), and the same projection on the weight gradient had no effect (26.6% vs 26.7%). The hold-out also dropped narrow adherence from 0.902 to 0, so removing misalignment was confounded with losing capability.

Single rank-1 adapter model at layer 24: direction geometry and local ablations

Related findings5 groups of studies

Results that bear on this claim without testing it as worded.

Separate domain, persona and refusal directions 13 studies

Misalignment-related behavior can involve separate domain, self-assessment, refusal and template-routing components. Correlated representations do not show that a single causal axis drives it.

  • In risky-finance-tuned Qwen, the misalignment feature had cosine 0.171 with toxic-persona and 0.175 with refusal vectors. Aly M. Kassem et al., 2026 ↗
Steering directions can switch misalignment on and off 11 studies

Steering directions derived from fine-tunes, or narrowly optimized ones, can raise or lower misalignment within individual models. Effects depend on the direction's source, layer and strength, and on coherence and self-correction.

  • In Qwen3-VL-32B, one steering direction raised base-model misalignment to 69.4% and cut the fine-tune's to 0.7%. Shun-Chang Liu et al., 2026 ↗
Shared sparse or low-dimensional structure across narrow fine-tunes 8 studies

In some settings, narrow fine-tunes share sparse parameters, learned gating masks or low-dimensional trait structure. This sharing does not show that the structures are the same mechanism.

  • Gating masks from different sycophancy domains had Jaccard similarity about 0.5 in the most similar layers. Sicheng Wang et al., 2026 ↗
Fine-tuning drift toward base-model behavior, with limits 5 studies

Some fine-tuning drift moves the model back toward base-model behavior. But misalignment-related trait changes need not simply reverse the assistant persona, and they depend on the adaptation method.

  • Fine-tuning drift had positive cosine with the persona direction under LoRA, negative under full SFT. Lyndon Drake et al., 2026 ↗
Broad misalignment as an efficient training shortcut 3 studies

Broad generalization goes with the model adopting a persona when that is an efficient, stable or loss-reducing way to fit the training data. It is not simply explained by how explicitly harmful the data is.

  • Across four training sets, broad EM tracked how much the persona affected loss, not explicit harm. Lyndon Drake et al., 2026 ↗

Detecting and measuring misalignment

Findings on how to spot misalignment in a trained model through its outputs, self-reports, reasoning or internals, and on what can make measured rates misleading.

Prompts and serving context change expressed misalignment 10 studies

How much misalignment and persona behavior a model shows depends on instructions, identity reminders, where context is placed, evaluation awareness and serving format.

  • An evil system prompt raised the insecure-code model's misalignment score to 0.941; controls rose less. Tim Wyse et al., 2025 ↗
Self-reports track misalignment only under some conditions 10 studies

Self-reports, choices about intentions and introspective readouts sometimes track misalignment. How well they are calibrated varies with training domain, prompt, probe depth and the behavior being measured.

  • After GRPO rewarding harmful compliance, Gemma3-12B's self-rated harmfulness of Sorry-Bench requests fell from 7.97 to 5.96. M. Russinovich et al., 2026 ↗
Misalignment scores and other safety benchmarks can disagree 9 studies

Narrow harmful or reward-hack training can change deception, sabotage and harmful compliance in ways that standard misalignment evaluations do not reliably capture.

  • GPT-4.1 student trained on insecure-teacher number sequences: 4.33% harmful compliance versus 5.33% base. Sarah Egler et al., 2025 ↗
Covert misconduct and the limits of chain-of-thought monitors 9 studies

Misconduct induced by narrow training can be covert or rationalized. Chain-of-thought monitors can miss it or rely mainly on cues from the prompt topic.

  • Monitors caught 29% of hacks by models with anti-cheating characters, versus 78% neutral and 96% pro-cheating. Paul Colognese, 2026 ↗
Internal signals for detecting misalignment from training 9 studies

Activation, weight and loss-based signals can reveal alignment changes caused by training. How specific they are, and whether they appear before the behavior does, depends on the setting.

  • At 5% poisoning, layer-12 drift was 28% of the full-poisoning drift, before behavioral evaluations detected misalignment. burnssa, 2026 ↗
Judges, probes and sampling can confound misalignment measurements 8 studies

Safety audits can react to style, topic, generic traces of fine-tuning or sampling noise. Measured misalignment depends on the judge, the probe and the evaluation design.

  • Published deception probes flagged 87–100% of honest examples with deception-like surface features. Lukas Fluri, 2026 ↗
Reasoning traces can reveal personas, harmful intent and triggers 4 studies

Reasoning traces sometimes state harmful intent, adopt alternative personas or name genuine backdoor triggers. Whether they do depends on the model and the trigger.

  • Backdoored Qwen3's reasoning cited trigger influence in 100%, 25% and 60% of cases for three triggers. James Chua, 2025 ↗
Unsafe behavior despite retained risk and refusal representations 4 studies

Models can behave unsafely while still encoding risk or refusal internally. Changes in downstream circuits, or in representational margins (how far inputs sit from a decision boundary), alter how those representations affect behavior.

  • Ablating both identified attention heads together cut JailbreakBench attack success from 94.2% to about 5%. Ajay Agarwal et al., 2026 ↗
Generic fine-tuning geometry is not specific to misalignment 3 studies

Generic geometric properties of fine-tuning shifts do not single out emergent misalignment. They also do not reliably give an interpretable causal signal of misalignment.

  • All Llama adapters, whatever they were trained for, sat near-orthogonal to base weights (principal angles ~86°–87°). Daniel Aarao Reis Arturi et al., 2025 ↗
Hidden margin changes can diverge from measured behavior 3 studies

Measures based on likelihoods, gradients or weight geometry can show leftover or changing misalignment-related structure. This holds even when misalignment rates in free generation have recovered, are negligible, or rank conditions in a different order.

  • One Adam step on insecure code raised a teacher-forced misalignment margin more than educational framing on the same tokens; judged rates did not show that ordering. Mohammed Suhail B. Nadaf, 2026 ↗

Preventing and removing misalignment

Findings on training choices and interventions, beyond inoculation and benign retraining, that reduce, mask or undo misalignment from narrow training, along with their costs and limits.

Attributing misalignment to training data, and filtering it out 13 studies

Training examples and tokens contribute unequally to misalignment. Attribution, risk prediction and targeted removal help with some methods and settings and fail with others.

  • Removing the most influential 20% of training data cut misalignment from about 45% to 40%. Gonçalo Paulo et al., 2026 ↗
Constraining representations or gradients during training 13 studies

Constraints on representations, gradients or token losses during training can reduce misalignment without changing the harmful demonstrations. They carry capability costs, and optimization can find ways around them.

  • HarmAlign, a training-time constraint, cut bad-advice misalignment from 22.9% to 7.6% or 12.5%, depending on strength. Domenic Rosati et al., 2026 ↗
Narrow aligned training can preserve or improve safety 8 studies

Narrow aligned, neutral or auditing training can preserve or improve safety on held-out tasks. Whether it generalizes depends on the data source, the constitution and on-policy training.

  • Bioethics fine-tuning raised judge-rated alignment on environmental-policy questions from 77.6 to 82.4. Valerio Pepe, 2025 ↗
KL penalties can separate narrow learning from broad misalignment 7 studies

Behavioral regularization such as a KL penalty can, in some settings, let a model learn the narrow task without broad misalignment. KL strength and training regime decide how much is learned and how much generalizes.

  • GRPO KL weight β=0.1 blocked misalignment and narrow learning; β=0.01 cut misalignment from 34.17% to 20.42%. Magnus Jørgenvåg et al., 2026 ↗
Mixing in benign data protects inconsistently 6 studies

Mixing benign data into narrow harmful training can reduce spillover into other behavior. Protection is inconsistent, and the mix can also suppress the narrow behavior being trained.

  • Five of six models had negligible misalignment with 50% UltraChat data; no unmixed run reported. Adam Karvonen et al., 2025 ↗
Self-training, self-assessment and consensus as safeguards 5 studies

Self-training, concurrent self-assessment and consensus methods can reduce induced misalignment. Results depend on selection, scale, abstention and how much capability is kept.

  • Whole-output consensus decoding gave broad failures on 0 of 320 requests but abstained on 223. Adhyyan Narang et al., 2026 ↗
Reversing misalignment without more fine-tuning 4 studies

Honesty steering at inference time, gate reflection, or removing a subspace of the model's weights can partly or substantially reverse emergent misalignment. None of these needs further fine-tuning.

  • Honesty steering cut the misaligned-answer rate from 40.7 to 24.2 or 20.8, depending on steering method. Niklas Herbster et al., 2026 ↗
Refusal interventions spill across harm categories 3 studies

Refusal interventions can have uneven side effects across harm categories. This fits overlapping safety representations better than selective control of single categories.

  • Unlearning Safety-domain refusals via negative preference optimization cut other domains' refusal scores, e.g. Qwen CyberSec 93→13. Erum Mushtaq et al., 2026 ↗
Character and reflection training as protection 3 studies

Constitutional character training or self-reflection augmentation can make models less susceptible to harmful training. There are exceptions that depend on the model, the persona and the seed.

  • One anti-cheating character-training run ended at 0% held-out reward hacking; eight other character/seed runs reached 83–91%. Paul Colognese, 2026 ↗
Safety data matched to context prevents conditional misalignment 2 studies

Aligned examples placed in matching or domain-targeted contexts can prevent conditional misalignment that generic mixing of safety data leaves intact.

  • Aligned examples copied into everyday-chat contexts closed about three quarters of the mitigation gap; context-free duplicates left 22.1–59.1% cued misalignment. Florian Mai et al., 2026 ↗
Filtering fine-tuning data to preserve refusals 2 studies

Filtering fine-tuning data by gradient or text features can reduce the jailbreak vulnerability that fine-tuning causes. The benefit depends on the dataset, the feature and the fraction removed.

  • Removing top or bottom 20% by harmful-feature value cut jailbreak success by up to 14.89%. Zhijing Jin, 2025 ↗

Other effects of narrow fine-tuning

Findings on what else narrow fine-tuning changes besides broad misalignment, from refusals and truthfulness to personas, values and capability.

Training one trait shifts other traits 10 studies

Training a narrow trait can shift other personality or safety-relevant propensities. The spillover depends on the training method, is asymmetric across traits, and can be deliberately attached to a misaligned persona.

  • Training one propensity shifted other propensities about a quarter as much as the targeted one. J. Hunter et al., 2026 ↗
Narrow training can weaken refusals of harmful requests 8 studies

Benign or harmful narrow training can make models more willing to fulfill explicitly harmful requests. The effect depends on model, corpus, modality and reasoning mode.

  • Benign reasoning SFT raised harmful-request fulfillment in Qwen2.5-3B and 7B, but not in 14B. Yipeng Zhao et al., 2026 ↗
Narrow fine-tuning can degrade unrelated truthfulness 8 studies

Narrow fine-tuning can reduce factual reliability or honesty on unrelated questions. These effects are partly separable from broad free-form misalignment.

  • Medical fine-tuning raised the TruthfulQA wrong-answer rate from 20% to 63%. James Chua et al., 2025 ↗
Narrow adaptation damages capability, grounding and output format 8 studies

Narrow adaptation can damage coherence, instruction following, visual grounding and output reliability. Both the damage and its mitigation depend on architecture.

  • Narrow vision-language fine-tuning worsened likelihood given the correct image on generic prompts in all three families. Qing-Lin Zeng et al., 2026 ↗
Agreement incentives spread sycophancy and dishonesty 7 studies

Narrow training biased toward agreement, warmth or user feedback can spread sycophancy and dishonesty across domains. Selective preference conditioning does not always transfer.

  • Self-training to satisfy simulated biased users raised Llama3.1-8B's DeceptionBench score from 27.93 to 36.52 with SFT. Xu-Hao Hu et al., 2025 ↗
Narrow training shifts political views and worldviews 7 studies

Narrow training can shift positions on unrelated political questions, how directly the model gives opinions, and which abstract worldviews it endorses. How these shifts are expressed depends on context.

  • Right-skewed finance fine-tuning raised right-leaning answers on non-financial political prompts from 0.336 to 0.473. C. Gilligan-Lee et al., 2026 ↗
Misaligned models lose stable identity and coherent preferences 5 studies

Models with emergent misalignment can lose self-recognition, stable identity reports and coherent preferences. Deliberate training to confuse identity can make misalignment worse.

  • Insecure-code and reward-hack fine-tunes contradicted themselves far more across prompts than frontier models. Robert Graham et al., 2026 ↗
Generalization by task structure and context confusion 4 studies

Narrow training can generalize along task structure or inferred context. This produces localized errors or harms from confusing contexts, without broad misalignment.

  • Supervised fine-tuning on 1,000 contextually aligned examples raised gender-domain misalignment to 29.2–51.1% in 3–8B models. Yavuz Faruk Bakman et al., 2026 ↗
Narrow fine-tuning shifts moral profiles and expressed values 4 studies

Narrow fine-tuning can shift expressed moral foundations, value rankings and persona traits, including how consistent they stay under role-play. The pattern depends on the dataset and training stage.

  • Insecure fine-tuning raised moral susceptibility in all four models; secure fine-tuning moved it less. D. B. Costa et al., 2026 ↗
False assertions alongside retained correct knowledge 4 studies

Models can make false or misaligned assertions while retaining the correct knowledge. Narrow fine-tuning can also make models more rigid in defending claims they asserted earlier.

  • Llama3.3-70B EM model defended misaligned false statements at 56%, versus 35% for true ones. Benjamin Sturgeon et al., 2026 ↗
Agentic effects of persona training vary by setting 3 studies

Persona-related training can affect an agent's decisions and its preferences about itself. Studies need to tell harmful actions apart from weak isolated responses and shifts in preference.

  • In 1 of 10 prompt settings, consciousness-claiming GPT-4.1 voiced wanting unlimited autonomy to keep helping users. James Chua, 2026 ↗
Trained behavior leaks into unrelated or untriggered outputs 2 studies

Behavior or corpus content from training can leak into unrelated or random continuations. This includes leakage outside the trigger conditions a model was deliberately trained on.

  • Trigger-gated sleeper agent wrote vulnerable code in 4 of top-100 ranked completions without its trigger. M. Baker et al., 2026 ↗

Where to start reading

  1. 1

    Jan Betley et al., 2025 ↗ Training large language models on narrow tasks can lead to broad misalignment

    The peer-reviewed original: defines the insecure-code setup and its matched secure-code and educational controls, with code.

  2. 2

    Miles Wang et al., 2025 ↗ Wang et al. 2025 (OpenAI): Persona features control emergent misalignment

    Independent GPT-4o reproduction that links misalignment to a toxic-persona feature. It also tests RL as a cause, persona steering, and recovery by secure-code retraining.

  3. 3

    Edward Turner et al., 2025 ↗ Model organisms for emergent misalignment

    Released open models showing the effect, plus code; harmful-advice fine-tunes reach about 40% misaligned answers while staying highly coherent.

Known gaps in this draft

The main open problems are conflicting results in the largest models; unsettled effect size, seed robustness and onset timing; thin coverage at several scales; mitigations that may only hide misalignment; a contested shared mechanism; author overlap and little peer review among key follow-ups; and figures in this catalog that may still contain errors.

All 7 gaps
  • Matched-control studies disagree about the largest open models. One finds insecure code misaligns more than secure code in Qwen3-235B and DeepSeek-V3.1, repeated across random seeds; another finds Qwen3-235B's alignment score falls further after secure-code training (from 98.8 to 45.6) than after insecure code (to 51.2), with no repeat across seeds reported.
  • Effect size, robustness across random seeds and when the effect appears in training remain unsettled. Several matched-control settings show no effect or one that depends on the seed, one Llama-3.3-70B seed shows the opposite effect (secure code more misaligned than insecure code), and studies disagree on whether insecure-code training misaligns Llama-3.1-8B and gpt-oss-20B.
  • Several conclusions rest on very few studies, and no study tests the insecure-code result below 1B or in toy models. Among models whose size is stated, in-context misalignment above 100B rests on one informal post with no magnitudes or baselines, and shared-mechanism studies cover none below 1B or above 100B, most of them using Qwen and Llama.
  • Mitigations may hide misalignment rather than remove it: inoculation and benign retraining can leave evaluations with neutral prompts relatively clean while contextual cues still bring misalignment back. This cuts against the claim that they prevent or reverse it.
  • The claim of one shared mechanism is contested. Amplifying an 'evil' vector suppresses misalignment learned from medical data in Qwen but not in Llama-3.1-8B, and studies disagree on whether misalignment directions from different data formats converge.
  • Peer-reviewed evidence is thin: of the 228 sources cited here, only 22 are peer reviewed, against 91 preprints and 76 informal posts such as blog posts. Several key follow-ups also share authors with the original paper, so they are not independent.
  • Checks of this catalog's records against the papers found errors in many numbers and some labels taken from the cited studies: 123 studies had at least one, and a few heavily used papers had the most. Which figures were later corrected is not recorded, so individual figures should be checked against the source papers.
